implementation_notes: Node's AsyncLocalStorage (stable since v16.4.0) is the context object for the event loop: one store is created per request with asyncLocalStorage.run(store, ...) at the HTTP boundary, propagates through promises, timers and I/O callbacks without any parameter, and is read with getStore() anywhere in the flow - the direct analogue of thread-local storage for asynchronous code. Framework request objects (Express req/res.locals, Fastify request decorations) are the explicit substitute when everything stays inside one handler, and a hand-rolled context-plus-factory object passed as an argument remains the honest design where async_hooks is unavailable, such as browsers or restricted edge runtimes.
pitfalls: enterWith() mutates the store of the current execution and keeps it for the rest of that execution, so it leaks across logically separate operations - prefer run(), which restores the previous store on exit.

Context is lost wherever the runtime cannot track a callback (a listener registered outside the run scope, a queue drained elsewhere), and a store kept on a module-level object silently becomes global state.
